What stays on the phone, and when the internet is used

• Your notes, drawings, PDFs, photos, recordings and settings are kept in this app's private storage on this phone.

• Text in photos and PDFs is read on the phone. Document scanning uses Google's scanner (Google Play services) on the phone.

• Voice typing uses your phone's speech service. Depending on the phone, that service may send the audio to its maker (for example Google) to turn it into text.

• The app uses the internet only when you ask: Back up to Google Drive (into a private app folder in your own Drive that only this app can see), and Clip page on a link (the app opens that one page). Nothing else is sent. There are no ads, analytics or tracking, and your notes are never used to train AI.

• A backup file is as private as the place you keep it; it isn't encrypted.

• App lock hides the notes on screen; it doesn't encrypt files, exports or shared copies.

• Deleting: empty the Trash to remove notes for good; uninstalling removes everything on the phone; Drive backups can be deleted in Settings › Backup.
